source.title: Adversarial Training Time Attack Against Discriminative and Generative Convolutional Models
source.authors: Subhajit Chaudhury; H. Roy; Sourav Mishra; T. Yamasaki

record.tranche_reason: The study reports how optimizers and regularizers affect test performance under an intentionally crafted training-time pixel attack, and qualifies generalization claims in that setting. It does not test the versions' ordinary natural-data training conditions.
record.gate_note: The attack is optimized to induce a training/test gap. The study's results on naturally trained models and cited results from other work are not rows. Figure-only optimizer and regularization outcomes are recorded without reconstructing values.
record.test_reason: The study deliberately optimizes training-data pixel perturbations to induce overfitting and evaluates optimizer resilience and regularization defenses against that attack. It does not independently measure the claimed behaviors arising without that induction. Its loss-surface interpolation also does not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness or generalization-gap ranking.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: crafted training-time pixel attacks degrade clean-test performance; SGD is more resilient than the tested adaptive methods; and the tested dropout and weight decay provide little protection. The authors also report sharper SGD solutions, impaired GAN reconstructions, and improved attack resilience with their proposed variational objective.
record.recipe_differences: The study deliberately optimizes class-wise pixel perturbations in training data to induce overfitting; it does not reproduce the listed studies' methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, attack strength (number of perturbed pixels), optimizer, regularization method, architecture, and input transformation affect reported outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Under optimized single-pixel training attacks, SGD has higher clean-test accuracy than Adam and RMSProp across the four datasets; Adabound has intermediate performance (Section VIII-G, Figure 8).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer choice affects resilience to deliberately crafted class-specific training-data pixel shortcuts.

fits_no_version.finding: Under single-pixel attacks, dropout probability 0.4 has little or no effect on clean-test performance. Weight decay of 0.01 gives marginal early improvement but similar final accuracy after 30 epochs (Section VIII-D, Figure 7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested dropout and weight-decay configurations provide little final protection against this training-time pixel attack.

fits_no_version.finding: Interpolation between SGD and Adam weights shows a sharper loss profile near SGD despite lower training and test losses (Section VIII-G.1, Figure 9). This is not magnitude-scaled perturbation sharpness, and lower test loss alone does not establish a smaller generalization gap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Directional loss-surface flatness need not identify the solution with better clean-test performance under crafted training-data attacks.

record.problems: Several relevant outcomes are presented only in figures, without values in the supplied text. Optimizer and regularization findings concern an adversarially modified training distribution and do not establish effects under standard natural-data training.
record.rows_left_out: No rows were kept because the reported optimizer and regularization results are specific to an intentionally induced training-time attack and do not measure the natural-data behaviors named by V4 or V6. Figure 7–9 results are summarized in fits_no_version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out generalization with the same architectures and training recipes.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD held-out performance under the specified tuning regimes without deliberately induced overfitting; broader tuning, optimizer switching, and decoupled weight decay.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipes that recover large-batch performance.
Dropout's held-out-error benefit outside the deliberately crafted attack, including dropout configuration, training-set size, and joint removal with weight decay.
Magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation tolerance, its correlation with generalization gaps at similarly low training loss, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Change the record's tests/T5 classification and its V4/V6 tested_not_extracted statuses. The empty row set is appropriate under the intentional-induction exclusion. Figures 7–9 are already declared in rows_left_out, so they do not require missing entries. Exact plotted values are unavailable in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and generalization on natural labels under standard training.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Ordinary training on natural data and the stated image-classification or language benchmarks; only outcomes under an induced pixel attack are reported.
Large-batch versus small-batch training under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout's effect on ordinary held-out error in the stated fully connected and convolutional classifier regimes; only attack resilience is assessed.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation sharpness and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and retraining.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
